summary: 惠帝崩后继位，好学博综，然东海王越专权；永嘉五年刘曜破洛阳，帝蒙尘，后于平阳被杀，西晋元气尽丧。
summary_en: Succeeding Emperor Hui, he was a student of wide learning, but the Prince of Donghai ruled; in the 5th year of Yongjia Liu Yao broke Luoyang, the emperor was carried off, and he was put to death at Pingyang — the strength of Western Jin was spent.

portrait.appearance_basis: 史载无形貌描写。画像宜表现好学而受制权臣的君主之态，衣冠从西晋末制。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 生
timeline.summary: 武帝第二十五子，封豫章王。
timeline.summary_en: Twenty-fifth son of Emperor Wu, enfeoffed Prince of Yuzhang.

timeline.title: 即位
timeline.summary: 惠帝崩，炽即位，改元永嘉。
timeline.summary_en: On Emperor Hui's death Chi took the throne and changed the era to Yongjia.

timeline.title: 东海王越辅政
timeline.summary: 东海王越专权辅政，帝拱手听命。
timeline.summary_en: The Prince of Donghai, Sima Yue, dominated the government, and the emperor folded his hands.

timeline.title: 刘聪继位匈奴汉
timeline.summary: 刘渊卒，刘聪继立，寇逼洛阳。
timeline.summary_en: Liu Yuan died and Liu Cong succeeded, pressing toward Luoyang.

timeline.title: 洛阳倾覆

timeline.summary_en: Liu Yao and Wang Mi broke Luoyang, burned the palaces, and slew over thirty thousand officials and people; the emperor was carried off.

timeline.title: 平阳遇害
timeline.summary: 帝被送至平阳，青衣行酒后为刘聪所杀。
timeline.summary_en: Brought to Pingyang, made to serve wine in servant's dress, he was put to death by Liu Cong.

bio_md:
# 晋怀帝 · 主要事迹

司马炽字丰度，武帝第二十五子。好学博综，永嘉之乱前以「冲素好文」著称，封豫章王。光熙元年惠帝崩，东海王越迎立炽即位，改元永嘉。帝即位后颇欲振作，然八王之乱方息，匈奴之祸已兴：东海王越专权辅政，帝拱手而已；越领兵出镇，忧惧交加，病卒于项。

永嘉四年，刘渊卒，刘聪继立，遣刘曜、石勒等寇逼洛阳；洛阳饥困，城中人相食。永嘉五年六月，刘曜、王弥等破洛阳，纵兵焚掠，百官士民死者三万余人，帝蒙尘被俘，先送至平阳，刘聪以「青衣行酒」辱之，建兴前遇害，年三十。西晋之首都洛阳，自此丘墟。

怀帝在位六年，非无志之主，然承八王之乱之弊，当胡骑叩关之势，中兴之业，无可措手。永嘉之乱与「衣冠南渡」并称，为西晋灭亡之标志：洛阳倾覆之后，中原板荡，晋室南迁，中国历史自此转入东晋南朝与五胡十六国并立之局。

> 参考：点校本《晋书》卷005《怀帝纪》、卷102《刘聪载记》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Chi, styled Fengdu, was the twenty-fifth son of Emperor Wu, a student of wide learning known for his quiet love of letters, enfeoffed Prince of Yuzhang. In the 1st year of Guangxi, on Emperor Hui's death, the Prince of Donghai brought him to the throne; the era was changed to Yongjia. He wished to act, but the War of the Eight Princes had barely ended and the Xiongnu storm was rising: the Prince of Donghai governed alone and the emperor folded his hands; Yue, marching out with the armies, died of worry at Xiang.

In the 4th year of Yongjia Liu Yuan died and Liu Cong succeeded, sending Liu Yao and Shi Le against Luoyang; the city starved until men ate men. In the sixth month of the 5th year, Liu Yao and Wang Mi broke in, burned and looted, and slew over thirty thousand officials and people; the emperor was carried off to Pingyang, where Liu Cong made him serve wine in servant's dress before putting him to death, aged thirty. The capital of Western Jin lay in ruins.

Six years on the throne, Chi was no man without spirit, but he inherited the wreck of the princes' war with the barbarian cavalry at the gate; there was no room for recovery. The Yongjia disaster and the "crossing of the caps and gowns south" mark the fall of Western Jin: with Luoyang in ashes and the Central Plains lost, the Jin house fled south, and the age of the Eastern Jin and the Five Barbarian Sixteen States began.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 5 ("Benji of Emperor Huai"), ch. 102 (records of Liu Cong).
